Inulat ng Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines na walang malaking pinsala ang Super Typhoon #UwanPH sa karamihan ng mga paliparang normal na ang operasyon ngayon.

“Initial inspections indicate that damages were primarily limited to ceilings, roofs, glass panels, and perimeter fences. Flooding was observed in some areas, with temporary disruptions to power and connectivity. 

CAAP has lifted NOTAMs (Notices to Airmen) for Bicol International, Masbate, Naga, Virac, Daet, and Cauayan airports. Baguio Airport has reopened, however Visual Flight Rules remain suspended due to poor visibility caused by heavy rains.”

Pero nananatiling suspendido ang operasyon ng Bulan Airport, Bacon Airport, Sangley Airport, Plaridel Airport, Iba Airport at Subic Airport. | RH 15 @JecelleRicafort, DZRH News

data.text:
SIERRA MADRE WEAKENS, DOES NOT FULLY PROTECT FROM STORMS

The Sierra Madre Mountain Range can weaken typhoon winds, but it does not completely shield northeastern Luzon from storms, the Department of Science and Technology said in a Facebook post.

Flooding and heavy rainfall often cause more damage than typhoon winds, the agency stressed, citing a 2023 study by Dr. Gerry Bagtasa and Dr. Bernard Alan Racoma in the Philippine Journal of Science.

Protecting the Sierra Madre from deforestation, mining, and other destructive activities due to its biodiversity and role as a natural barrier is crucial, the researchers emphasized.

📸 DOST Philippines via Ian Peter Guanzon #CDNDigital

data.text:
Super Typhoon Fung-wong slammed ashore on Sunday in the northeastern coast of the Philippines, where the massive storm had already left at least two people dead and forced more than a million people to evacuate from flood- and landslide-prone areas, officials said.

The typhoon blew into Dinalungan town in Aurora province Sunday night after setting off fierce rain and wind in northeastern Philippine provinces all day from offshore, with sustained winds of up to 185 kph (115 mph) and gusts of up to 230 kph (143 mph).

The biggest typhoon to threaten the Philippines in years, Fung-wong could cover two-thirds of the archipelago with its 1,800-km-wide rain and wind band, forecasters said.

data.text:
Super Typhoon Fung-wong leaves trail of destruction in the Philippines
.
Super Typhoon Fung-wong battered the Philippines on Sunday (November 9), leaving at least two people dead and forcing the evacuation of one million residents before making landfall. Eyewitness footage captured towering waves slamming into Catanduanes’ shores, sending torrents of seawater flooding through coastal streets.
.
By Monday morning (November 10), entire communities in the north were reeling from the storm’s destruction. Drone footage from Nueva Ecija revealed submerged farmlands and homes as rivers burst their banks under relentless rainfall. Power cuts and blocked roads left several areas isolated as locals emerged to assess the widespread damage.
.
Now moving across the South China Sea towards Taiwan, Fung-wong remains a severe threat. The state weather agency warned of continuing heavy downpours, fierce winds, and dangerous coastal swells. The storm — the 21st to strike the Philippines this year — hit just days after Typhoon Kalmaegi, which claimed more than 200 lives.
.

data.text: It appears there's an all of government response underway in the Philippines to assess, report and respond to damage caused by Typhoon #UwanPH. There are many power and communications outages; widespread road and bridge infrastructure damage caused by flooding reported; many landslides; plus significant crop damage across Luzon and points south. Casualty numbers are still low, but search and rescue operations are still ongoing in places. Death and injury reports are likely going to climb as individual localities report into national authorities. So far, they are low. Similarly, there is likely more damage than is being seen at the moment as some areas are still without power or communications. In all, things could be much worse, but still, quite a few people have lost homes to flooding or to landslides. It may take 24 hours to gain a fuller sense of the overall impact on the country

A lot of people seem think  this whole "Japa" syndrome, is their hustle, their glow-up ticket to maple syrup dreams in Canada or Big Apple bagels? Nope—that's the script they've written for you. The same puppets pulling strings in Ukraine's Maidan (Euromaidan), India's media wars (Newslaundry), and Philippines' press crackdowns are now flooding your TL with sob stories of Naija expats "making it" abroad. And the puppet master? Pierre Omidyar, the eBay billionaire playing God with your future through his Omidyar Network (ON)—a $1.5B+ slush fund that's less "philanthropy" and more CIA cutout for the great African brain drain. Buckle up; this ain't vibes, it's the uncut playbook.

Let's start at the source: ON isn't crowdfunded by do-gooders; it's Pierre and Pam Omidyar's personal war chest, bloated on eBay billions (Pierre's net worth? $10B easy). They launched it in 2004 to "bend the arc" toward "shared power"—code for engineering "democracy" wherever the war machine smells oil or veto power. But peel the label, and it's a revolving door to the spook squad. ON doesn't take outside cash; it pumps it out to NED (National Endowment for "Democracy"—Reagan's CIA rebrand) and USAID ops that toppled Yanukovych in Ukraine 2014 (ON bankrolled protest NGOs like Center UA). In India, they fund ADR for "electoral reforms" that smell like a color revolution prep, and Rappler in the Philippines? ON-backed media-CIA psyop. Grayzone nailed it: Omidyar's network is the soft-power hammer for regime change, hiring intel-adjacent firms like Frontier Design (U.S. Army Special Forces clients) to build AI "ethics" that really means surveillance states. Pierre's Iranian roots (parents fled the 1979 revolution) got him Dalai Lama cozy (an ex-CIA asset), and his PayPal roots? Born in DARPA's Surveillance Valley. Coincidence? Or a blueprint for global control?

Shift focus to Naija: Why flood the motherland with "abroad life" porn when Nigeria has 200M+ potential? Enter Zikoko—the pop culture trap house that's got everyone's timelines hooked on quizzes, memes, and their sneaky "Citizen" corner. ON's fingerprints? All over it. Zikoko is juiced by Omidyar grants, turning your fave vibe site into a social engineering front. Not the whole site o—just enough to seed the poison. "Citizen"? It's a Japa factory, churning out "Abroad Life" tales that glorify the grind: Ken (49), bolted 20 years back, dodges racism in the West but swears off Naija return—"I'd rather settle in other African spots." Uyai (41) sells her Lagos pads for Ivy League dreams, ends up "from grace to grass" in the U.S.—but hey, at least it's "free." Gabriel (31) flees for queer freedom, hits soul-crushing loneliness and discrimination—yet the moral? "Escape Nigeria."

It doesn't stop there: Boye ditches UNILAG mid-degree for U.S. permanent residency—"chasing the American dream." Lola (25) ghosts her family in Canada since 2016, feels like a "stranger" on Naija visits. Obi (27) bounces four cities in ten years, spills "hard truths" on the Japa hustle—but the hook? Keep chasing that unsettled glow. Even #EndSARS refugees get the treatment: "Lekki massacre lit the fire to leave." One lady shares a UK room with seven randos after ditching a "comfortable" Naija life—struggle porn at its finest. And the kicker? A Naija queen does the unthinkable for U.S. citizenship after five years waiting—whatever it takes, right?

This isn't organic scroll bait; it's engineered exodus. ON's playbook: Fund the fun (Zikoko's quizzes keep you hooked), then drip the despair disguised as hope. Result? Massive brain drain on steroids—Nigeria has lost 15k+ doctors to the UK alone since 2020, engineers to Canada, techies to Silicon Valley. Why? Depopulate the Giant of Africa, scoop the talent for Western machine shops, leave the homeland hollowed out for resource grabs (oil, lithium, rare earths). CIA's wet dream: No strong Nigeria means no BRICS pivot, no AU muscle, just compliant compradors. Omidyar has already bankrolled BudgIT for "transparency" that exposes corruption but ignores the puppeteers. Tie it to the big lie: "West = freedom," while they build walls and raid your remittances.

Uncut truth? This is hybrid warfare—memes as missiles, stories as sleeper cells. Pierre is NOT saving souls; he's scripting the great replacement in reverse: Export your best, import their bots. Follow the money—it leads to ON's vaults, NED's shadows, and Zikoko's servers.  They want Nigeria to be the next Ukraine: Fund the youth rage (#EndSARS echo), amplify the exit ramps, watch the regime wobble. But we can flip this!

Wake up! UnJapa your minds. Boycott the bait, build the motherland: Tech hubs in Abuja, not Austin; farms in Ogun, not Ontario. Audit these "philanthropists," demand ON's grant logs, flood X with counter-stories of Naija thriving. 

What Nigeria has, isn't true independence. This needs to change, and it will require every single one of you. Balkanization only leaves everyone vulnerable, and the entity with the wildest military arsenal will swoop in and pick it all apart. I'm not asking you to kumbaya and love everyone, but the citizens MUST band together to achieve total success in vanquishing these parasites.

WAKE UP!

The storm is here—stay and own it.
